invariants.note: Single SWAP kernel unaffected; accuracy binding remains runtime/coupler policy.
No files, parsing, formats, paths or file units enter the binding.
Application requirement, temporal allocation and interface allocation remain explicit policy data.
No persistent physical column state is added.
No solver scratch is added to persistent state.
No memory-layout constraint is introduced.
Binding does not alter checkpoint, trial, commit or rollback semantics.
No warm-start or recomputation rule is changed.
Accuracy allocations do not prescribe calendar units or a fixed timestep.
No coupling-window duration is hard-coded.
Coupling accuracy policy is explicit and composable with runtime coupling.
Interface head tolerance remains distinct from hard flux action/reaction.
No mass-conservation tolerance or relaxation is introduced.
Interface sensitivities remain first-class and unaffected.
Accuracy binding adds no full SWAP trajectories.
Policy objects are lightweight and compatible with MultiSWAP runtime composition.
No 1:1 groundwater-cell mapping assumption is introduced.
Deep-vadose ownership remains external to SWAP.
No component-storage transition semantics are altered.
No dependency on a specific soil-water solver is introduced.
SWAP process physics remains shared and unmodified.
No HeadCalc-internal dependency is introduced.
Application/coupling accuracy policy remains distinct from physical options and solver physics.
No hidden fallback or unbounded-cost solving rule is introduced.
Reference mode remains available and unchanged.
Separate provenance for application, temporal and interface allocations is explicit and diagnosable.
Binding cost occurs only when direct groundwater coupling is configured.
Project/application policy composition remains outside the kernel.
No hidden project, calendar, file-format or external-model default is introduced.
Change explicitly audited against all architecture invariants.
